issue.body: ### I have searched the existing issues, both open and closed, to make sure this is not a duplicate report. - [x] Yes ### The bug **Description:** When viewing database backups in the Immich Web UI, the time as well the relative time (e.g., “in 59 minutes”) is incorrect when the time zone of the frontend is different from UTC. The timestamp in the backup filename is generated in the server’s local timezone (e.g., Europe/Berlin), but the frontend previously parsed it as UTC, causing the time to appear in the future or past depending on the timezone offset. **Environment:** - Server timezone: Europe/Berlin (set via TZ env variable) - Docker and server time are correct - Immich version: v2.5.6 The filename and the timestamp from the server. ``` -rwx------+ 1 root root 17M Feb 24 23:02 immich-db-backup-20260224T230229-v2.5.6-pg14.19.sql.gz ``` And the environment and date reported from the docker container. ``` docker exec immich_server env | grep TZ TZ=Europe/Berlin ``` ``` docker exec immich_server date Tue Feb 24 23:10:38 CET 2026 ``` **Problem:** In MaintenanceBackupEntry.svelte: ``` const dateMatch = filename.match(/\d+T\d+/); if (dateMatch) { return DateTime.fromFormat(dateMatch[0], "yyyyMMdd'T'HHmmss", { zone: 'utc' }).toLocal(); } ``` This code extracts the timestamp from the filename and parses it as if it were in UTC, then converts it to the browser's local time. However, the timestamp in the filename is actually in the server's local time (Europe/Berlin), not UTC. This means if your browser is in the same timezone as the server, but the code treats the time as UTC, it will always appear "in the future" by the UTC offset (e.g., 1 hour for CET, 2 hours for CEST). **Solution:** Change the parsing zone from 'utc' to dynamic based on the server's TZ if available otherwise use the fallback as UTC. ### The OS that Immich Server is running on Synology, x86 ### Version of Immich Server v2.5.6 ### Version of Immich Mobile App v2.5.6 build.246 ### Platform with the issue - [x] Server - [x] Web - [ ] Mobile ### Device make and model _No response_ ### Your docker-compose.yml content ```YAML # # WARNING: To install Immich, follow our guide: https://docs.immich.app/install/docker-compose # # Make sure to use the docker-compose.yml of the current release: # # https://github.com/immich-app/immich/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml # # The compose file on main may not be compatible with the latest release. name: immich services: immich-server: container_name: immich_server image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release} # extends: # file: hwaccel.transcoding.yml # service: cpu # set to one of [nvenc, quicksync, rkmpp, vaapi, vaapi-wsl] for accelerated transcoding volumes: # Do not edit the next line. If you want to change the media storage location on your system, edit the value of UPLOAD_LOCATION in the .env file - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/data - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro env_file: - .env environment: TZ: Europe/Berlin ports: - '2283:2283' depends_on: - redis - database restart: always healthcheck: disable: false immich-machine-learning: container_name: immich_machine_learning # For hardware acceleration, add one of -[armnn, cuda, rocm, openvino, rknn] to the image tag. # Example tag: ${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}-cuda image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release} # extends: # uncomment this section for hardware acceleration - see https://docs.immich.app/features/ml-hardware-acceleration # file: hwaccel.ml.yml
